pensamiento:
I'm checking QUS-001, which meets the role-action-benefit form. QUS-002 is borderline on atomicity: it asks to disable both biometrics and the password to log in only with a PIN, so it bundles two deactivations, though it could also read as one goal. I'm leaning toward treating the security concern as the main problem rather than the atomicity question.

I'm going through the remaining user stories in the list. QUS-003 has a minimal scope and passes. QUS-004's benefit, entering faster, is a valid value and passes too. For QUS-005, the story prescribes a specific PIN mechanism rather than just the need, but I'm not going to flag that as a defect, since it's a business decision. QUS-006 is ambiguous: "entrar más rápido" has no measurable target, so I'll mark it as a major defect.

I'm checking QUS-007 for conflicts with other stories. Biometric login is already requested in BAN-01 and BAN-03, and this story would remove it along with the password, so I'm marking it as a blocking defect. QUS-008 and QUS-009 pass, and INV-001 passes too, since the only dependency is the conflict already covered under QUS-007.

I'm moving through the rest of the checklist now. INV-003 looks not estimable, since the 4-digit length is stated but attempts, lockout, password replacement, and recovery are all undefined, so I'll mark it as a major defect. INV-005 has no acceptance criteria at all, which is a blocking defect. I'm also starting to check DOR-001 for dependencies on the device biometric service and the auth service.

I'm treating DOR-001 as a defect since the removal of biometric and password login touches the existing authentication service and the device biometric API, and neither is mentioned. DOR-002 also fails because there are no rules for attempt limits, lockout, or PIN changes, even though the 4-digit length is given. I'm now starting on DOR-003, the non-functional requirements, since login is a critical path.

I'm checking the security checklist next, starting with BM-001 on authentication, where dropping the password and biometrics leaves only a 4-digit PIN, which is a blocking issue. BM-002 looks like a major gap since session expiry and re-authentication aren't defined. I'm also weighing BM-004 on how the PIN would be stored locally, which the story doesn't address.

I'm weighing whether BM-005 applies, since removing the password and biometrics changes the user's login credentials, which could count as a change to customer data. It's not clear-cut, so I'm inclined to flag it as a major gap rather than a definite defect.

I'm weighing BM-006 next: the PIN entry screen is changing, so the accessibility check applies, and I'm leaning toward flagging it as a minor gap. BM-007 also looks like a gap, since login failures and service errors aren't defined, which I'd mark as a major defect. I'm now looking at BM-008 on platform behavior, since disabling biometrics touches device functions.

I'm checking the remaining items on the security checklist, and BM-009 on personal data doesn't apply since no new personal data is involved. BM-010 on SUGEF also looks not applicable, because changing the login method isn't a financial operation or customer-facing financial information. Since there are already many defects, I'm weighing how to estimate this story, given that the missing rules make an estimate unreliable.

I'm weighing whether the scope is clear enough to estimate, since removing biometric and password login with a 4-digit PIN is describable even though many rules are missing. I'll look up the estimation scale and reference points before deciding whether to return the story with its defects registered.

recomendaciones.texto: Definir el factor de autenticación del ingreso. Quitar biometría y contraseña deja solo un PIN de 4 dígitos, lo que debilita la autenticación actual. Indicar si el PIN es el único factor o si se mantiene un segundo factor o reautenticación para operaciones sensibles.

Resolver el conflicto con BAN-01 (ingreso con biometría) y BAN-03 (login biométrico), que exigen ingreso con huella o rostro. Esta HU pide desactivarlo. El producto debe decidir cuál prevalece antes de reformular.
Reemplazar 'entrar más rápido' por una medida observable, por ejemplo un tiempo máximo de ingreso medido en condiciones definidas.
Aclarar el alcance para estimar: reglas del PIN (intentos fallidos, bloqueo, cambio y recuperación), si la contraseña se elimina por completo o solo como opción de ingreso, y pantallas afectadas.

Agregar criterios de aceptación en formato de reglas o lista de verificación, cada uno con un resultado observable. Por ejemplo: con PIN correcto se ingresa a la app; con PIN incorrecto se muestra error y se cuenta el intento.
Mencionar las dependencias: el servicio de autenticación actual y la API de biometría del dispositivo que se desactiva, en iOS y Android.
Definir las reglas: cantidad de intentos fallidos permitidos, qué pasa al superarlos (bloqueo y desbloqueo), y reglas de cambio o vencimiento del PIN.
Declarar al menos un requisito no funcional medible para el ingreso, como tiempo de respuesta o disponibilidad.
Definir el comportamiento de la sesión tras el ingreso con PIN: expiración por inactividad, reautenticación al volver de segundo plano y cierre de sesión.
Indicar dónde y cómo se almacena el PIN o su verificador en el dispositivo (almacén seguro del sistema operativo, sin texto plano).
Indicar el registro de auditoría del cambio en el método de ingreso (quién, cuándo, dispositivo), sin datos sensibles en claro.
Indicar que la nueva pantalla de PIN considera accesibilidad (lector de pantalla, contraste, tamaño de texto) según WCAG 2.1 AA.
Definir qué pasa sin conexión, con tiempo de espera o con error del servicio durante el ingreso con PIN.
Indicar el comportamiento en iOS y Android al desactivar biometría, incluidas las versiones mínimas soportadas.
